title: Pattern's Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is charged on market capitalization rather than on revenue or assets
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.3.1.2.1.1.1 sets the terms in one line: "Pattern will pay 0.50% of its market capitalization per year in USDS."

The choice of *base* is the substantive decision, not the rate. Market capitalization is a valuation measure, so the fee behaves like a property tax on the Agent's perceived worth rather than an income tax on what it earns. Consequences follow directly: the obligation is highest exactly when the token is most expensive, it is owed even in a year of zero profit, and it can be inflated or deflated by market moves the Agent does not control. Against that, it is far harder to manipulate than reported revenue and requires no audit of the Agent's books — an oracle-style number the ecosystem can compute externally.

Denominating payment in **USDS** rather than PATTERN is the second decision. It forces a real outflow into the stablecoin Sky is stabilizing, rather than letting the Agent settle its ecosystem obligations in its own paper. Combined with the permanent ban on emissions beyond Genesis Supply, this means upkeep must be funded from actual earnings or reserves.

The fee is not yet operational: A.6.1.1.6.2.3.1.2.1.2.1.1 states that "the process to pay 0.50% of Pattern's market capitalization per year in USDS will be specified in future iterations of the Pattern Artifact." The obligation exists before the mechanism that discharges it — including any definition of how or when market capitalization is measured.
description: 0.50% of market cap per year, payable in USDS, so the levy tracks the market's valuation of the Agent and rises in a bull market even when the Agent is earning nothing.
